events.title: Charles Lindbergh Lands in Paris
events.description: Charles Lindbergh completed the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight, landing the Spirit of St. Louis at Le Bourget Field near Paris after about 33.5 hours in the air, having departed from Roosevelt Field, New York, on May 20.
events.significance: The flight made Lindbergh an international hero and sparked a surge of public and commercial interest in aviation, helping launch the modern air travel industry.

events.title: American Red Cross Founded
events.description: Clara Barton and a group of associates established the American Red Cross in Washington, D.C., modeled on the International Red Cross movement founded in Geneva.
events.significance: The organization became a leading provider of disaster relief, blood services, and aid to military members in the United States and abroad.

events.title: FIFA Founded in Paris
events.description: The Fédération Internationale de Football Association was founded in Paris by representatives from seven European national associations: France, Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, and Switzerland.
events.significance: FIFA grew into the global governing body of association football and organizes the FIFA World Cup, one of the most widely watched sporting events in the world.

events.title: First Democratic National Convention Opens
events.description: The first Democratic National Convention began in Baltimore, Maryland, where delegates nominated Andrew Jackson for a second term and selected Martin Van Buren as his running mate.
events.significance: It established the national party convention as the method for choosing presidential candidates, a practice that shaped American politics for generations.

events.title: Death of Henry VI of England
events.description: Henry VI, the Lancastrian king of England, died in the Tower of London, widely believed to have been murdered on the orders of the victorious Yorkist king Edward IV, on the night of May 21.
events.significance: His death effectively ended the Lancastrian claim during the Wars of the Roses and consolidated Yorkist control of the English throne.
